Q: Maximize/Restore buttons in the title bar are disabled in a QMainWindow - pyqt5 A:

@musicamante's comment is very helpful and deserves to be an answer.

I had a similar problem with a QWizard, which does not show the minimize and maximize buttons in the titlebar by default. Setting the window flags did show those buttons. But the maximize button remained disabled. The QWizard sets some inherent value for its maximumSize property. Once I restore that property to the default value, the maximize button shows and is enabled.

Unlike the OP, I did not use Qt Designer. So in my derived wizard constructor, I did the following.

class FooWizard( QWizard ):
  def __init__( self, parent = None ):
    super( FooWizard, self ).__init__( parent )

    self.setWindowFlag( Qt.WindowMinimizeButtonHint )
    self.setWindowFlag( Qt.WindowMaximizeButtonHint )

    # Setting the flag above does show the maximize button,
    # but it remains disabled if the wizard thinks that a maximum size is specified.
    # Thus I must restore maximum size to the default.
    # https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qwidget.html#maximumSize-prop says:
    # By default, this property contains a size in which both width and height have values of 16777215.
    self.setMaximumSize( 16777215, 16777215 )

    self.addPage( FooWizardPage1() )
    ...

Q: Disable UITextField Predictive Text A:

For me it worked also setting the spellCheckingType as no (iOS 15, Swift 5+)

textField.autocorrectionType = .no
textField.spellCheckingType = .no

Q: ImageJ macro not working on other computers A:

There are some aspects of your macro code that appear being questionable:

  1. Never ever use fixed thresholds. Always use a suitable automatic threshold scheme. For the green channel of your sample image this could be setAutoThreshold("Intermodes dark");

  2. It makes no sense to first call an automatic threshold scheme and then set a fixed threshold.

  3. The call setOption("BlackBackground",true); must precede the thresholding.

  4. Be aware of the fact that if you use "show=Masks" with run("Analyze Particles...", ...); the resulting image will always be shown with inverted LUT. Therefore it is a good idea to then call run("Invert LUT");.

Q: Sub loop via while within primary loop A:

You can do this entirely in a single SQL query, you don't need all this PHP iteration.

$stmt = mysqli_prepare($dbc, '
    INSERT INTO paycor (client, mlo)
    SELECT c.client, c.mlo
    FROM commission AS c
    JOIN pay_post AS p ON FIND_IN_SET(c.filename, p.filename)
    WHERE p.paid_on = ?');
mysqli_stmt_bind_param($stmt, "s", $today);
mysqli_stmt_execute($stmt);

As another answer mentioned, it would be better if you normalized the pay_post table so there are separate rows for each filename (this might need to be a new table, to avoid duplicating the other columns). Then you would not need FIND_IN_SET(), which can't be optimized with indexes.

Q: What type of object is $<drivename>: (such as `$code:`) in Powershell? A:

What you're seeing is namespace variable notation, which is a variable-based way to access the content of items in PowerShell drives whose underlying provider implements content-based access (i.e., implements the IContentCmdletProvider interface).

Terminology and documentation note:

  • As of this writing, the docs briefly explain namespace variable notation in the conceptual about_Scopes help topic, albeit without using that term and, somewhat confusingly, discuss it in the context of scope modifiers; while namespace qualifiers (such as $env:) are unrelated to scope modifiers (such as $script:), they use the same basic syntax form, however.[1]

The general syntax is:

${<drive>:<path>}       # same as: Get-Content <drive>:<path>

${<drive>:<path>} = ... # same as: Set-Content <drive>:<path> -Value ...

The enclosing {...} aren't necessary if both the <drive> name and the <path> can syntactically serve as a variable name; e.g.:

$env:HOME  # no {...} needed

${env:ProgramFiles(x86)} # {...} needed due to "(" and ")"

In practice, as of Windows PowerShell v5.1, the following in-box drive providers support namespace variable notation:

  • Environment (drive Env:)
  • Function (drive Function:)
  • Alias (drive Alias:)
  • FileSystem (drives C:, ...)
  • Variable (drive Variable:) - though virtually pointless, given that omitting the drive part accesses variables by default (e.g., $variable:HOME is the same as just $HOME).

Of these, the Env: drive is by far the most frequently used with namespace variable notation, even though most users aren't aware of what underlies an environment-variable references such as $env:HOME.

On occasion you see it used with a file-system drive - e.g., ${c:\foo\file.txt} or ${c:file.txt} - but the fact that you can only use literal paths and that you cannot control the character encoding limits its usefulness.[2]

In general, namespace variable notation allows interesting uses; e.g.:

PS> $alias:foreach  # Get the definition of alias 'foreach'
ForEach-Object

PS> $function:prompt # Get the body of the 'prompt' function
"PS $($executionContext.SessionState.Path.CurrentLocation)$('>' * ($nestedPromptLevel + 1)) ";
# .Link
# https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=225750
# .ExternalHelp System.Management.Automation.dll-help.xml

# Define a function foo that echoes 'hi' and invoke it.
PS> $function:foo = { 'hi' }; foo
hi

Note:

  • Because ${<drive>:<path>} and ${<drive>:<path>} = <value> are equivalent to
    Get-Content -Path <drive>:<path> and Set-Content -Path <drive>:<path> <value>, paths are interpreted as wildcard expressions (because that's what -Path does, as opposed to -LiteralPath), which can cause problems with paths that look like wildcards - see this answer for an example and a workaround.

[1] Previously, the feature wasn't documented at all; GitHub docs issue #3343 led to the current documentation, albeit not in the way that said issue proposed.

[2] Additionally, in the cross-platform PowerShell (Core) 7 edition, as of v7.5.x, it doesn't work by default on Unix-like platforms, because /, the only file-system PowerShell drive defined there by default, cannot be used as a drive spec; e.g., ${/:file.txt} does not work. See GitHub issue #3245 for a discussion.

Q: How to disable new 'modal window' in VSCode A:

To disable this, you need to toggle a specific setting in your settings.json or the Settings UI.The FixOpen Settings (Ctrl + ,).Search for: workbench.editor.openSettingsInEditor (or workbench.settings.editor).Ensure it is set to ui or json (the default "editor" mode).However, if you are referring to the Floating/Centered layout that appeared in recent updates, add/change this in your settings.json:

"workbench.editor.showTabs": "multiple",
"workbench.settings.useSplitJSON": false
